newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB says Michigan unit in line.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB says Michigan unit in line.

text.p: National Australian Bank Ltd (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Thursday the profit performance of its U.S. unit, Michigan National Corp, was in line with expectations.

Michigan reported an operating profit of A$158 million, before amortisation of goodwill, in the 11 months to September 30, 1996. "Michigan National performed in line with our expectations," Argus told reporters at a press conference.
Argus said he planned to use the U.S. unit, which it bought for US$1.56 billion a year ago, as a test-bed for new technologies the bank planned to introduce in the future.

Argus said Michigan National was a great research and development centre of new banking technologies as its was part of the Integrion Financial Network venture with 14 other banks and International Business Machines Inc.

"If that (Integrion) proves as well as what we think it will it will certainly be a great adjunct to our group activities," Argus said. The Integrion venture plans to offer a range of electronic financial services in the U.S. and Canada.
Argus said NAB also plans to hold the first trial of the Mondex payment smart card through its U.S. unit next year before introducing it to its Australian operations.
"We are very happy with what they are doing there (Michigan National) and it will be a great platform going forward," Argus said.
NAB has a small stake in Mondex, the rest of the London-based group is owned by other banks, ATT Corp and payments company MasterCard International.
NAB earlier reported a 6.8 percent rise in net profit to A$2.1 billion in the year to September 30, 1996.
At 3.50 p.m. (0450 GMT), NAB shares were 25 cents higher at A$14.17.
